transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Reese (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Lumina Head of Security), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Ravi Desai (Data Privacy), Leah Ortiz (SRE, note-taker)

Summary (auto-gen): quick security posture discovery focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, and data retention for evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Agreed next steps: share compliance artifacts, schedule technical deep dive and perf benchmark.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this deal. We've got Priya our SE and Miguel CSM. Thanks Lumina team for carving out time.
00:18 Aisha: Hi, thanks. I'm Aisha, head of security. We've been evaluating a few vendors and want to focus this call on security, compliance and networking constraints.
00:30 Tom: Tom from platform, we'll be looking at integration points and perf for real-time features.
00:40 Jordan: Great; goal is to understand your requirements around SOCtwo, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
00:55 Priya: Quick note I might jump in with technical specifics — e.g., how we do key management, audit trails, and network topologies.
01:10 Aisha: Top three blockers for us: SOC 2 Type II evidence, support for SAML-based SSO with SCIM for provisioning, and the ability to ensure that PII never leaves our VPC without explicit encryption keys.
01:27 Jordan: Understood. On SOC2 we are Type II — I'll send the report. For ISO, we have ISO 27001 artifacts as well, not sure if full cert is required but we can share relevant controls.
01:40 Aisha: Good. Also need to confirm retention windows and ability to redact or disable retention for certain routes. Our legal team will want clear SLAs on data deletion.
01:55 Ravi: From privacy perspective we need KMS integration, ideally customer-managed keys, and a chain of custody for keys. Will that be supported in Hosted?
02:10 Priya: Short version: Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS by default; we offer Dedicated and Private where you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) — HSM/KMS integrations via IAM and specific key rotation policies. In Dedicated you can configure your own KMS in most cloud regions; Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer keys with direct HSM integrations.
02:35 Tom: Any differences in how KV cache or temp tokens are stored between modes? We care about ephemeral state on GPU hosts.
02:48 Priya: We treat KV cache as ephemeral in the runtime — not persisted to long-term storage. For Hosted we may cache in memory; for Dedicated and Private you get more control and can disable persistent caches. There's occasional wording in our docs where KV cache is spelled K-V cach in autogenerated outputs, apologies for that.
03:05 Aisha: Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs with export to our SIEM and retention of 7 years for certain events. Is that doable?
03:20 Miguel: We have configurable audit logging — you can stream audit events to customer-owned S3 or to syslog/CloudWatch in Dedicated/Private. Hosted can stream to customer sinks via our log-export connectors; for strict immutability requirements we recommend Dedicated with write-once storage.
03:40 Ravi: What events are logged? Prompt texts? Token-level logs? We need to minimize storing raw prompt data for regulated PII.
03:55 Priya: By default we log metadata and request IDs, timestamps, model/version, latency and error codes. Storing full prompt/response is optional and must be explicitly enabled. For Hosted we have controls to disable prompt retention and to redact PII using a redaction pipeline. For Dedicated/Private you control whether prompts are persisted at all.
04:18 Aisha: How about SSO/SAML and RBAC — we use Okta and want SCIM for provisioning and granular role controls so our engineers can't access production prompts.
04:35 Jordan: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based at org, project and route levels; we can lock down routes to roles, and integrate with SSO groups for automatic mapping. Priya, can you add details?
04:48 Priya: Yup. We map Okta groups to Redwood roles. You can define custom roles and permissions: read-only, admin, developer, etc. For stricter separation, Dedicated and Private let you enforce network-level access and restrict console access with IP allowlists.
05:05 Tom: For our real-time latency needs, if we go Dedicated will we still get the same performance as Hosted? This is more security than perf but interlinked.
05:20 Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity on GPU pools; performance is predictable. Hosted has multi-tenant optimization that can deliver low latency, but Dedicated avoids noisy neighbors and gives SLO guarantees. For strict compliance+perf tradeoff many customers pick Dedicated for production.
05:40 Aisha: On encryption, we need AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit, plus customer-managed keys. Also key rotation policies.
05:52 Priya: We support TLS1.2+ and AES-256. KMS integrations allow rotation; for BYOK you control rotation schedules and revocation. For Hosted customers can opt into a BYOK path for enterprise tiers — we can share the flow doc.
06:10 Ravi: Can you describe the deletion flow? If we request data deletion, how quickly is that actioned and what logs prove it happened?
06:24 Miguel: Deletion is actionable via API and console; for Hosted we have a deletion job that runs across storage tiers and we return deletion receipts. For Dedicated/Private, deletion is immediate in your environment; we provide signed attestations and audit entries. We'll share the deletion SOP.
06:44 Aisha: Regulatory question: ISO evidence and penetration tests — do you have third-party pentest results and ongoing vulnerability scanning reports?
06:57 Jordan: Yes, third-party pentest summaries are available, and we have continuous scanning and patching processes. I'll include the summary with the SOC2 pack.
07:10 Tom: Networking — can we keep all egress inside our VPC? We need to ensure outbound is limited and TLS terminated inside our network if we do Private.
07:25 Priya: Private supports fully air-gapped or VPC-hosted control plane; Dedicated gives VPC peering and private link options. Hosted uses managed endpoints; for sensitive egress we recommend Private so traffic never traverses public internet.
07:45 Aisha: Data residency — we're US+EU presence; need to ensure EU customer data stays in EU for banking customers.
07:55 Jordan: We have region pinning by default and can pin model serving to EU regions. For Private we can deploy fully in your EU cloud region. We'll capture the exact services you must keep in region.
08:15 Ravi: Are service account keys auditable? We want narrow-scoped service accounts and rotation enforced.
08:28 Priya: Yes, we support short-lived tokens via our auth service and fine-grained service accounts with rotation. We integrate with customer IAM for federated access as well.
08:45 Aisha: Regarding tokenization or redaction — can Redwood run a redaction layer before any storage? For example, auto-PHI redaction on inputs.
08:58 Priya: We have an optional pre-processing pipeline that can redact PII/PHI using configured rules or a customer-provided regex set. That pipeline can run in Dedicated/Private for max control.
09:15 Tom: Any known limitations on model variants when running in Private? We have a set of smaller open models and one large LLM we want to serve; will all models be available?
09:30 Priya: Most open models we support; for some newer architectures there are kernel/compilation differences, we may need to validate. Model availability in Private depends on licensing; we can ship a validated model bundle for Private deployments.
09:50 Aisha: About retention — we need to be able to set route-level retention to zero for certain flows (e.g., support chat) but retain for others for 90 days. Is that configurable?
10:05 Miguel: Yes, retention is route-level. You can set per-route policies, and in Hosted we enforce those via our retention service; Dedicated/Private you have full control and can set to zero or long-term archival.
10:25 Ravi: On audit trails, we need signed logs. Can you create tamper-evident logs or append-only storage?
10:36 Priya: We can stream logs to customer-controlled append-only stores (e.g., S3 with object locking) and sign events. For Hosted we provide cryptographic hash chains for critical events if needed.
10:55 Aisha: Who sees prompt content at Redwood for debugging? We require that only a small SRE-debug role can see raw prompts and only under approved access requests.
11:10 Jordan: Access to raw prompts is strictly controlled, and we maintain access request workflows with approvals and audit trails. We'll share the policy.
11:25 Tom: If we start a pilot, can we run smoke tests with a subset of traffic, and can Redwood guarantee no data leakage to other tenants?
11:40 Priya: For pilot we recommend Dedicated sandbox or Private. We can guarantee isolation at runtime and can disable multi-tenant shared caches. We'll also provide a benchmark harness for your engineers.
12:00 Aisha: One last thing: legal will want indemnity clauses and specific data processing terms. Miguel, can you flag that to the contracts team?
12:12 Miguel: Yep, I'll loop in contracts and share a draft of the pilot T&Cs.
12:22 Jordan: Quick recap — Jordan to send SOC2/ISO/pentest summary; Priya to schedule technical deep dive and benchmark; Miguel to share pricing and pilot contract; Lumina to send network diagram and data classification.
12:40 Aisha: Thanks all. We should reconvene after we review the docs and once the technical deep dive is scheduled.
12:50 Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up via email and attach the artifacts.
13:00 End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: Some auto-generated parts mislabel product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicted"), and acronyms like SAML/SAML spelled inconsistently. There were small transcription artifacts in technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V catch"). We preserved the conversational flow and action items.
